pages.text: Addendum for $(l:structures/heart_chambers)$(c)$(o)Heart Chambers$().$(br)$(br)These Heart Chambers feel like an alternative to the Great Bodies. While those are closer to a superficial recreation of the human body, the chambers are reminiscent of a body's function and internal ecosystem. There is a heart in the middle, seemingly 'powering' the entire construct, with the additional rooms being close to organs working on

processing their own resources. I do admit that these correlations are lackluster at best, since in practice the plague's nature of recreating the past still strikes through. For example, one of the side rooms can sometimes feature a piece of a mineshaft made with Bondknot planks. Meanwhile another room type can have a piece of the End in it (which is fascinating in itself, as it highlights the transmutational capacity of the Risus). From my perspective - and with no true insight into

the inner workings of the Risus - it looks like the plague is missing a sort of 'focus'. It gives the impression of having multiple goals but lacking the factor by which to only invest into one at a time. This is speculation at best for now though, as it's mainly conjecture from my observations.
